decision: No shared IMF relationship-position substrate extracted during TASK-219
evidence_compared: TASK-218 IMF PIP/CPIS reporter-counterpart portfolio positions
TASK-219 IMF DIP/CDIS reporter-counterpart direct-investment positions
extraction_rejected_reason: TASK-218 and TASK-219 establish that the representation pattern repeats and remains operationally sufficient, but the stable contract is still narrow and source-specific semantics differ: PIP has accounting/sector/counterpart-sector portfolio instrument semantics; DIP has DV_TYPE, inward/outward direction, net assets/liabilities basis, instrument, entity, and official-vs-counterparty-derived data semantics. A helper extracted now would likely become generic IMF SDMX/relationship machinery rather than a small proven source-specific boundary.
future_extraction_gate: Consider only a narrow IMF counterpart-position helper after another relationship campaign or a maintenance pass shows repeated non-semantic duplication with a testable contract for metadata acquisition, active artifact promotion, raw manifest inventories, release/as-of derivation, and relationship accounting reports. Keep provider-series semantics task-local.
measurable_friction_observed: Campaign implementation reused the PIP pattern mechanically, but required task-local changes to key dimensions, selected indicator families, value-status attributes, and metadata interpretation. No canonical collision, source identity ambiguity, or idempotence failure occurred.
repeated_relationship_responsibilities: counterpart economy preserved in source-scoped indicator identity and attributes
provider-derived as-of identity used as fact as_of_date
explicit missing cells distinguished from whole-series absence
same-run idempotence and rolled-back later-as-of coexistence checks
